newsitem.title: USA: First Union cites higher fee income in Q3.
newsitem.headline: First Union cites higher fee income in Q3.

text.p: First Union Corp cited higher fee income as a contributor to higher operating earnings in the third quarter of 1996.
Fee income excluding securities transactions rose 28 percent to $598 million from $466 million a year ago.
Net interest income rose six percent to $1.28 billion from $1.21 billion a year ago.
Average net loans were $90.5 billion in the third quarter cmopasred to $86.0 billion a year ago.
First Union's non-performing assets were $825 million or 0.89 percent of net loans and foreclosed properties at the end of September, versus $818 million or 0.95 percent a year ago.
Annualized net charge-offs were 0.64 percent in the third quarter of 1996, compared with 0.33 percent in the third quarter of 1995.

Operating earnings of $442 million or $1.60 per share diluted. A one-time assessment of $86 million aftertax for the Savings Association Insurance Fund (SAIF) reduced net income for the latest period to $356 million or $1.29 per share.

First Union said that going forward it expects to realize a net annual benefit of $35 million pretax from reduced SAIF premiums. First Union said it expects to apply the saving to business-related initiatives designed to enhance revenues by increasing the selection of products, services and distribution channels.

First Union said that during the third quarter of 1996 it sold $8 billion of securities as part of a corporate balance sheet management process. First Union said the action will result in a higher-yielding earning asset mix going forward.
